story.thematic: What survival costs when the past remains unexplained

turns.narration:
The rigger’s wrench turns another fraction under your question. You stand beside the cargo crate, boots steady on the grating, as the hose trembles against his glove. “Quartz,” he says. “I didn’t get a clear look at the person behind the tanks.”

He lifts his knee from the crate and wipes his fingers on a rag, leaving a dark streak across the cloth. The pale chip remains beside the wrench. His eyes stay on the coupling as he resumes tightening it, while the sealed tanks block the far side of the bay from view. A faint comms crackle brushes the reactor hum.

turns.action: I inspect the pale quartz chip beside the wrench, studying its edges and any res
turns.narration:
You lift the pale quartz chip from beside the wrench and roll it under the docking bay’s strip lights. Fine gray grit clings to one beveled edge; a greasy smear marks the opposite face, but no readable stamp or clear source shows on its surface. You set it down and crouch beside the crate, sweeping your gaze over the grating and the narrow gap beside the sealed tanks.

A fresh crescent of dust has been scuffed from the floor near the crate’s far corner. You follow it to the gap, where a cobalt thread snags on a rough bolt head, and reach for the opening before the rigger shifts his crate into place. “Need that moved?” he asks, wrench still in hand. You hook the thread free, but the crate scrapes across the grating and crushes the loose dust marks beneath its edge.

The figure in the cobalt work coat appears at the service-corridor mouth, one hand pressed to the wall as they look back toward you. Then they turn and move out of sight. The rigger lowers the crate the rest of the way, and the broken trail ends under its weight.

turns.narration:
You plant your shoulder against the crate and shove. Its weight drags over the grating with a harsh scrape; your boots hold, and the crate slides clear of the crushed dust trail. The gap beside the sealed tanks opens wide enough for you to reach into it.

Beyond the gap, a narrow service hatch stands ajar. A strip of cobalt fabric is caught at its lower hinge, and a clean bootprint marks the dusty threshold—an unexpected opening in the cluttered bay, but no sign of where the figure went. Behind you, the rigger grips his wrench and looks from the shifted crate to the hose coupling. “That’s my work clear now,” he says, then turns back to the line.

A dry tap sounds from inside the hatch, followed by the faint clatter of something metal being set down. The cobalt thread trembles against the hinge in the ventilation draft.

turns.action: I crouch beside the ajar service hatch and examine the cobalt fabric and clean b
turns.narration:
You crouch at the open hatch and pinch the cobalt fabric free from the hinge. Its weave is coarse, stained with hydraulic fluid; a loose white filament clings to the torn edge. Beside it, the clean bootprint has a narrow heel and a rectangular notch across the sole. You trace the notch with one gloved fingertip, then lean toward the dark corridor. “What did you just set down?”

A pause, then the scrape of a shifting boot. “A coupling key,” the person answers from inside. “It’s on the deck.” No face appears beyond the hatch. You draw back, catching the hatch’s sharp edge across your glove; a shallow cut opens at the knuckle, and a bead of blood marks the cobalt weave. At the bay’s workbench, the rigger keeps both hands on the hose coupling. “Keep the crate clear,” he says without looking up, while the reactor hum fills the space between you and the unseen figure.

turns.action: I shove the service hatch wide and lunge into the dark corridor, bracing against
turns.narration:
You shove the service hatch wide and lunge into the dark corridor, bracing your forearm against its sharp edge. Your fingers close around the coupling key just before the cobalt-coated stranger’s hand reaches it. The stranger jerks back, shoulder striking the wall; in the cramped passage, their elbow drives into your side.

Pain tightens your breath. Blood wells through the torn fabric at your flank and warms your skin beneath the suit. The stranger keeps their face turned away, one palm raised between you and them. “You got it,” they say, voice low and clipped. “I only needed the key.” They retreat deeper into the corridor, leaving their next step hidden in the dark.

Behind you, the rigger’s wrench rasps against the hose coupling in the docking bay. The coupling key presses cold and heavy into your bloody hand; the open hatch leaves the repair bay exposed, and the stranger remains somewhere beyond its threshold.
npcs: Unidentified person in a cobalt work coat (active, neutral)

turns.action: I clamp a hand over the wound in my flank and charge after the cobalt-coated str
turns.narration:
You clamp your hand over the wound and charge down the corridor. Your shoulder catches the cobalt-coated stranger across the back before they can reach the next recess. You drive them against the bulkhead; their boots skid on the grating, and the coupling key stays clenched in your other hand. The stranger’s hood slips aside, exposing a narrow face and a fresh scrape along the jaw. They don’t strike back. One hand grips the corridor rail; the other stays open and empty.

The impact pulls at your flank. Blood slicks your palm and darkens the edge of your suit, but the stranger is pinned within reach, their breath coming fast through the recycled air. A small stamped mark shows on the key’s handle, matching a fresh impression in the dust beside their boot. “I told you, I needed it,” they say, avoiding your eyes. “The mark’s from the fitting.” They twist toward the shadowed recess, testing your hold without forcing it.

From the docking bay, the rigger calls, “Kimora! I need that key—the line’s slipping, and the hatch is open!” His wrench clatters against the grating. The corridor’s pressure seal hisses behind you; the stranger remains under your shoulder, and the bleeding has not stopped. The rigger waits with the repair, while the passage beyond the recess stays dark.
npcs: Unidentified person in a cobalt work coat (active, neutral)

turns.action: I wrench the cobalt-coated stranger away from the shadowed recess and slam them
turns.narration:
You wrench the stranger from the recess and slam them against the bulkhead. Their shoulder hits metal; your flank knots with pain, and the coupling key stays clear of their grasp. You shove off toward the docking bay, one hand pressed to the wound. Each step jars your ribs. By the time you reach the rigger, blood has spread beneath your palm.

“Key. Now,” the rigger says, reaching for it. He keeps his other hand on the trembling hose coupling. “If the line slips, the hatch seal loses pressure.” You place the key in his hand. He seats it in the fitting and bears down; the line steadies with a hard metallic knock. The stranger stops at the bay threshold, hands visible, keeping distance. “The key fits the bleed screw too,” they say. “Look at the fresh scoring on its tip.” The rigger glances at the mark, then holds the key under the strip light. The dust impression and fitting still need a closer comparison.

Your breath catches as you straighten. The service hatch remains open, and the rigger sets his wrench down to wrap your flank with a clean strip of cloth. Beneath the pain, your grip loosens; the doubts come back with it, small and hard to shut out. The stranger waits by the threshold while the blood seeps through the first layer of the dressing.
npcs: Unidentified person in a cobalt work coat (active, neutral)

judge.weakness: The narration assigns the player character returning doubts and a loosening grip beyond the stated action.

turns.action: ## I was being cautious, not aggressive
turns.narration:
You guide the stranger away from the recess without striking the bulkhead, keeping the coupling key beyond their reach. Your injured flank tightens beneath the blood-darkened wrap as you cross the grating toward the docking bay. The rigger holds out a grease-streaked hand. “The line’s slipping. A delay can drop pressure at the hatch seal and put everyone in this bay at risk.” You place the key in his palm. He turns to the fitting and sets the coupling with short, controlled movements.

The stranger stays beside you, hands visible. “I needed the key to open the secondary line’s bleed screw,” they say. “You can check the scoring against the fitting.” The rigger pauses, then compares the fresh marks on the key with the screw; their shapes correspond, but the dust impression beside the stranger’s boot remains an incomplete match. He finishes securing the coupling, then points you toward the workbench. “Sit. Let me clean that wound before we compare the marks properly.” The stranger waits under your watch as the rigger reaches for the medical roll.
